verdict: pass for reviewed face-scale issue, with visible pose steps
scope: Chrome local preview, 1× native previous preview/current side-by-side. Reviewed 270→292.5→315→337.5→000; forward and backward paused stepping; sampled automatic forward playback; 2× diagnostic.

observations.270→292.5: The eyes and face rise as the head looks upward. A visible pose step remains, but the eye shapes and sizes remain broadly comparable and the chin rises with the face against a steady laptop. At 1× this reads more as a head lift than the conspicuous whole-face growth seen in earlier candidates.
observations.292.5→315: The farther eye opens wider and the face turns more frontal; the face broadens modestly. The eye separation and mouth shift along with the turn. There is no similarly conspicuous whole-face enlargement at native size.
observations.315→337.5→000: The face turns toward center, and the 337.5→000 seam remains materially steadier than the prior preview.
observations.reverse: The same pairs were checked in reverse with the previous-frame control; the upward pose step is visible but the face does not appear to collapse in scale.
observations.playback: Automatic playback ran and successive snapshots showed 292.5, 315 and 337.5. This screenshot-based inspection sampled the live loop rather than providing a continuous visual recording.

residual: The 270→292.5 lift is a noticeable discrete pose step; 292.5→315 includes visible widening of the farther eye. These are judged acceptable direction and pose changes at 1×, not a claim of perfectly smooth motion.
reused: The parent reports only 292.5 changed relative to full-v05-b, with other atlas pixels and preview controls unchanged. Prior checks of other directions, four-quadrant follow, idle/blink, themes and 2× responsive layout were not repeated.
limitations: Browser preview only; candidate was not installed or checked in native Dot.
Actual playback was sampled via screenshots; no continuous video was observed or recorded.
